item.title: 2027: 2Baba backs ‘rig and die’ slogan, demands severe penalties
item.description: Nigerian music star, Innocent Idibia, popularly known as 2Baba, has backed the controversial “rig and die” slogan associated with the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), saying anyone caught manipulating election results in 2027 should face severe punishment. The singer, however, cautioned against innocent people being victimised in the process, insisting that elections should not be treated as warfare. He made the remarks on Thursday during an interview on Nigeria Info 99.3, where he described Nigeria’s political atmosphere as tense and said the slogan reflected growing public frustration over the country’s situation. “You know, when the situation gets to a certain point, like right now, we’re on a very mountainous keg of gunpowder right now. Desperate times make people make some kinds of statements. “The statement sounds correct, right? It sounds correct. It should be like that, actually. For the circumstances. Like, if you rig, the punishments will be very severe to deter people from rigging,” 2Baba said. The singer said he saw nothing wrong with the slogan, arguing that stringent penalties would discourage electoral malpractice. “The statement itself is ‘rig and die’. I don’t see anything that’s wrong with it. It’s like saying embezzlement and die. Now, there’s that penalty for embezzlement in China,” he said. 2Baba also called for severe consequences for kidnappers, particularly those targeting schools, arguing that the absence of adequate deterrence had allowed criminal activities to persist. “We’re in a state where we need serious deterrence for anybody who kidnaps in our schools to face serious consequences, so that others will not do it. Because it’s getting too much and people are just getting away with everything,” he said. The ‘African Queen’ crooner said the slogan reflected the level of frustration among Nigerians but warned against punishing people without evidence of wrongdoing. “For me, the statement itself shows the level of frustration. It shows the level of how things have gone bad. So, for me, I don’t see anything wrong with that statement. “I just don’t want innocent people to get caught up in the process of this,” he added. During the interview, the presenter recalled 2Baba’s longstanding advocacy for peaceful electoral participation, including his message urging Nigerians to vote rather than fight during elections. Asked about Nigerians who might sell their votes because of economic hardship, the singer described the situation as unfortunate, noting that people facing difficult conditions could easily become vulnerable to manipulation. He also called for proper reorientation, urging Nigerians to address internal challenges rather than allow external interests to influence the country. The “rig and die” slogan has featured prominently in political discussions ahead of the 2027 general elections, particularly among supporters of the NDC and its presidential candidate, Peter Obi. item.title: CeBIH, NIMC to explore digital identity for financial inclusion, growth
item.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Committee of e-Business Industry Heads (CeBIH) and the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) are set to explore how digital identity can drive financial inclusion, trust and economic growth at the 2026 CeBIH Annual Conference scheduled for December 1 and 2 in Lagos. The conference, themed “Digital Identity: A Catalyst for Financial Inclusion, Trust and Growth,” will bring together policymakers, regulators, financial services leaders and technology innovators to examine the role of identity infrastructure in Nigeria’s digital financial ecosystem. Speaking at a press conference on the theme of the conference, Chairman of CeBIH, Mrs. Abidemi Asunmo, said the future of financial services and the broader digital economy depended significantly on reliable, secure and accessible digital identity infrastructure. “A trusted digital identity ecosystem has implications far beyond registration and identification. It can help address some of the structural barriers to financial inclusion.’’ Gbolahan Oluwatobiloba, Lagos State Coordinator, NIMC, said identity was the foundation of economic development, security and trust. “Identity is the foundation of everything, not just the financial sector, the security sector or the identity ecosystem. When you remove identity, your security will be affected, because how do you secure people you don’t know?” he said. Vice Chairman of CeBIH and Chairman of the Conference Planning Committee, Abednigo Ugwueke, said participants would examine how trusted digital identity could improve customer onboarding, strengthen Know Your Customer processes, enhance identity verification, reduce fraud and expand access to financial services. The conference is expected to feature key government and industry personalities, including NIMC Director-General, Engr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote; Executive Chairman of the Nigeria Revenue Service, Dr. Zach Adedeji; National Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, Dr. Vincent Olatunji; and Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service, Kemi Nanna Nandap. Kayode Olubiyi, Head of Digital Payments, UBA, representing the CeBIH Advisory Council, said customers increasingly prioritised security and trust in banking. The post CeBIH, NIMC to explore digital identity for financial inclusion, growth appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UNICEF, NGE, Lagos govt to tackle child survival, education challenges
item.description: By Ch ioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh Stakeholders, yesterday, called for stronger collaboration among government, the media, private sector and communities to address challenges threatening child survival, education and development in Nigeria. The stakeholders include the United Nations Children’s Fund, UNICEF, Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, Lagos State Government and Airtel Nigeria made the call at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium themed: ‘Every Child Alive, Thriving and Learning: A Shared Responsibility’ in Lagos. Speaking at the event organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the NGE and Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, DAME, President of the NGE, Mr. Eze Anaba, said the responsibility of ensuring that Nigerian children survived, received quality education and realised their potential rested on all stakeholders, not government alone. Anaba cited a UNICEF report indicating that 18.3 million Nigerian children were out of school, describing the figure as alarming and calling for urgent collective action. “In a country of over 200 million people, 18 million-plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming; it’s a collective responsibility,” he said. He challenged media organisations, private sector players, community leaders and parents to examine their contributions towards addressing the problem. “Have we reminded the government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” he asked. Anaba urged stakeholders to develop an action plan with specific commitments, stressing that annual commemorations must translate into measurable improvements in children’s lives. Earlier, UNICEF Chief of Communication, Advocacy and Partnership, Ms. Lone Hvass, said: “Survival, education and learning are deeply interconnected. A child who is out of school is denied much more than education. He or she is denied opportunities for protection, participation and the possibility of realising their full potential. “The media does much more than report on children’s issues. Media helps determine which issues receive public attention, which voices are heard, which assumptions are challenged, and which movements are followed through,” Hvass said. She urged journalists to move beyond episodic coverage and headlines to sustained reporting that connects individual experiences with systemic challenges, provides evidence and exposes gaps in policy implementation. Sanwo-Olu Also speaking, Lagos State First Lady, Dr. Claudiana Sanwo-Olu, said children were not merely beneficiaries of government policies but individuals with rights, aspirations, talents and opinions whose voices deserved to be heard in decisions affecting them. item.title: CBN appoints Murtala Mohammed acting MD of Keystone Bank
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has appointed Mr. Murtala Mohammed as Acting Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of Keystone Bank Limited. The appointment, announced on Thursday night, took effect on November 26, 2026, with Mohammed succeeding Mr. Hassan Imam. In a statement, the CBN Director of Corporate Communications and Investor Relations, Mr. Michael Akuka, said the appointment was made in exercise of the powers conferred on the apex bank by the Banks and Other Financial Institutions Act, 2020. He said the appointment was consistent with the CBN’s mandate to promote a safe, sound and stable financial system. “The appointment is consistent with the CBN’s mandate to promote a safe, sound and stable financial system,” Akuka said. The CBN reassured depositors, customers and other stakeholders that Keystone Bank remained fully operational, with banking services continuing as normal and depositors’ funds secure. “The CBN wishes to reassure depositors, customers and other stakeholders that Keystone Bank Limited remains fully operational, with banking services continuing as normal and depositors’ funds remaining secure. “The CBN remains committed to safeguarding depositors’ interests and ensuring the continued soundness and stability of Nigeria’s banking sector,” the statement said. item.title: 2027 election: Makinde may succumb to Atiku; I wish he’s with us — Bwala
item.description: Special Adviser to President Bola Tinubu on Media and Policy Communications, Daniel Bwala, has expressed hope that Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde would join the ruling All Progressives Congress and support Tinubu’s re-election in 2027, saying he would prefer the governor to align with them rather than former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar. Bwala warned that Makinde would betray Southern Nigeria if he backed Atiku in the 2027 presidential election, arguing that the presidency should remain in the South for eight years. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Bwala said he believed Makinde could eventually align with Tinubu, but expressed concern over the governor’s reported political dealings with Atiku. “Seyi Makinde, I have a belief in me that at some point he would even join Asiwaju, but let’s assume he doesn’t. The people he’s leading are not stupid. Power needs to remain in the South for eight years,” he said. Bwala said Makinde’s support for Atiku would amount to a betrayal of the South, given the region’s interest in retaining the presidency beyond Tinubu’s first term. “If he is going to succumb to Atiku Abubakar, he’s betraying the people of the South,” he said. Asked why he believed Makinde might support Atiku, the presidential aide claimed the arrangement had already been agreed to in principle, adding that events would confirm his assertion. “It is already agreed in principle and you will see what I am saying,” Bwala said. He also questioned Makinde’s chances if the governor decided to contest the presidency independently, arguing that he would struggle to defeat Tinubu in Oyo State. Bwala warned that such a move could damage Makinde’s political future. “That means his political career will be dead forever. Now, let’s assume he’s going to stand on his own to become president. How can Seyi defeat Asiwaju in Oyo State?” he said. The presidential aide also ruled out the possibility of either Atiku or Peter Obi stepping down for the other ahead of the election, saying both politicians had strong commitments to their supporters. Bwala said Obi’s supporters, particularly members of the Obidient Movement, expected him to contest the presidency, arguing that withdrawing for another candidate would amount to betraying their trust. “Peter Obi is running, if you ask obedient members, they’ll say because they believe Obi himself must be the president of Nigeria. That is his legitimacy. If Peter Obi now stops running and goes to another person, he has betrayed the trust. He has betrayed the covenant,” he said. He added that Obi was unlikely to step down for another candidate. item.title: Fountain of Life Church challenges bench warrant against Pastor Jimmy Odukoya
item.description: The Fountain of Life Church has raised concerns over the issuance of a bench warrant against its Senior Pastor, Jimmy Odukoya, by the Lagos State High Court, questioning the procedure leading to the order. In a statement dated November 26, 2026, the church said the development followed proceedings before Justice O. O. Adewunmi-Oshin, which also culminated in the judge’s recusal from the case. The church claimed that Odukoya had not been formally served with the restraining order, originating processes and accompanying documents, either personally or through substituted service, as directed by the court. It also alleged that directives contained in the court’s orders of November 18 and 23 concerning the service of the documents remained unfulfilled. According to the church, its legal representatives had already filed a Notice of Appeal and two separate motions challenging the orders, their enforcement, the court’s jurisdiction and the contempt proceedings. The church further claimed that the matter was not listed on the court’s cause list for November 26 and that members of the media were asked to leave the courtroom before the bench warrant was issued. It said the warrant was issued without the court first determining the pending applications, after which the presiding judge recused herself. “These developments occurred within eight days of the initial ex parte order and before 1 December 2026, the date originally fixed by the court for mention,” the statement said. The church described the circumstances as raising serious questions about due process, fair hearing and the administration of justice. It added that its lawyers were challenging the orders and related procedural and jurisdictional issues before the appropriate courts, including the Court of Appeal. Clarifying the implications of the warrant, the church said its issuance did not amount to a conviction or a final determination of the substantive leadership dispute. The church also maintained that Odukoya remained its duly appointed Senior Pastor and Chairman of the Board of Trustees, describing the position as part of the issues being pursued through the judicial process. It urged members and the general public to remain calm, united and prayerful, adding that it would exhaust all available legal remedies within the Nigerian judicial system. item.title: Sexual violence: UK, Mirabel Centre push for stronger protection, Justice for survivors
item.description: *Mrs Sanwo-Olu hails centre’s 10,000-Survivor Care Milestone By Henry Ojelu THE United Kingdom and the Mirabel Centre have called for stronger protection, sustained support and access to justice for survivors of sexual and gender-based violence in Nigeria. The British Deputy High Commissioner in Lagos, Mr Jonny Baxter, and founder of the Mirabel Centre, Itoro Eze-Anaba, made the call on Thursday at a reception and panel discussion in Lagos to mark the centre’s milestone of supporting more than 10,000 survivors of sexual violence. The event, held as part of the 2026 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence, also featured the launch of the centre’s publication, The Survivor Experience: A Voice That Matters. Speaking on the theme, “A Milestone of Care, A Call for Sustained Support & Justice,” Baxter said the achievement deserved celebration but stressed that sexual violence remained a serious issue requiring sustained attention and commitment. He said: “We want to celebrate 10,000 survivors, but we also want to ensure that many more people are able to access the professional support and services they need.” Baxter emphasised the importance of placing survivors’ experiences at the centre of interventions, saying their voices were essential to understanding their challenges and improving access to support and justice. He reaffirmed the UK’s commitment to ending violence against women and girls through development partnerships and collaboration with governments and civil society organisations. He also disclosed that the UK would soon host an international summit on technology-facilitated gender-based violence, noting that emerging forms of abuse required new approaches and solutions. Earlier, Eze-Anaba acknowledged the contributions of the British Council, the Department for International Development and the British High Commission to the establishment and growth of the centre. She said the British High Commission funded the centre’s first three years and continued to support its work through partnerships and advocacy opportunities. Describing the milestone as more than a numerical achievement, she said the centre remained committed to delivering services with dignity and respect. “Today is not about public relations for the Mirabel Centre. It is about the services we provide and how those services are shared in a dignified manner for survivors,” she said. Eze-Anaba said the centre regularly sought feedback from survivors and had engaged an independent consultant to assess its services, identify gaps and recommend improvements. She thanked the centre’s partners and funders, assuring that it would continue to provide compassionate care where survivors’ voices mattered. item.title: Igbokoda crash: Tinubu approves N100m, three-bedroom houses for victims’ families
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi President Bola Tinubu has approved three-bedroom flats in Abuja for the families of the 25 people who died in the October 5, 2026 Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash. He also announced the award of the sum of N100 million to the families of each military personnel who died in the crash, separate from the houses. The President made the announcement on Thursday during a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony held in honour of the victims of the NAF ATR 42 aircraft accident. He said the houses, located in the Renewed Hope Housing Project in Abuja, would be allocated to the immediate families of the deceased military personnel and civilians who were aboard the aircraft. Tinubu described the housing allocation as a demonstration of the nation’s appreciation for the sacrifices of the fallen personnel. “As a tangible expression of the nation’s gratitude, I approve the allocation of three-bedroom flats in the Renewed Hope Housing Project in Abuja to the family of each of the military personnel who lost their lives in this accident. “No home can ever replace the one you have lost, but they gave their lives for Nigeria, and Nigeria will give their family a home,” he said. The president pointed out that the gesture would also be extended to the immediate families of the civilians on board the aircraft. “In addition to the flats, these officers would receive from this government N100m each,” he said. He assured the bereaved families that the government would remain committed to supporting them beyond the memorial ceremony. “Long after the wreaths have faded, our commitment to these families must remain evergreen,” Tinubu said. The president also assured Nigerians that the October 5 aircraft crash would be thoroughly investigated, promising that the findings would inform improvements in military and civilian aviation safety. “I assure the grieving nation that this accident will be thoroughly investigated. We will seek answers. We will learn the lessons. We will strengthen our military and civilian aviation safety standards. Our operational procedures and our institutional accountability will be strengthened. “We owe them the truth, and we will honour that debt,” he said. Tinubu further reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving the welfare, safety and operational capacity of the Armed Forces through modernisation, training and better equipment. “A nation that asks its sons and daughters to fly into danger must give them the best wings it can build,” he added. The president urged the bereaved families to remember the deceased for their service and contributions to the country, assuring them that their sacrifices would remain in the nation’s memory. The October 5 accident claimed the lives of 25 people, including military personnel and civilians. item.title: 2027: Siakpere charges Okpe leaders to mobilise support for Tinubu, Oborevwori
item.description: …As Uko urges peace, unity, stronger grassroots mobilisation A chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Chief John Ewhubare Siakpere, has called on political leaders and stakeholders in the Aghalokpe axis of Okpe Local Government Area to unite and intensify grassroots mobilisation to secure victory for President Bola Tinubu, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and other APC candidates in the 2027 general elections. Siakpere, a member of the Delta State APC Campaign Council, made the call on Thursday when he hosted APC leaders and stakeholders from the Aghalokpe axis at his country home, urging them to put aside personal differences and work collectively for the success of the party. The APC chieftain, who is the Omo-Eni of Okpe Kingdom and a member of the Delta State APC Campaign Council, said Okpe’s political influence would depend largely on the ability of its leaders to speak with one voice and mobilise support at the grassroots. He urged the people to work for the re-election of President Tinubu and Governor Oborevwori, stressing that the party must secure victory at all levels in 2027. According to him, Governor Oborevwori’s decision to lead Delta State into the APC had further strengthened the party’s political standing, making it imperative for leaders and members to rally behind his administration and support its re-election bid. He said winning elections required more than political declarations, insisting that party leaders must maintain regular contact with the people, understand their concerns and take the APC’s message to every community. On the economic reforms of the Tinubu administration, Siakpere acknowledged the hardship Nigerians were experiencing, particularly the rising cost of food, transportation and other essential commodities. He, however, urged party leaders to explain the rationale behind the reforms, including the removal of fuel subsidy, while also emphasising the need for the government to ensure that the measures translate into tangible improvements in the lives of citizens. He noted that the savings from subsidy removal had increased the resources available to governments to meet their obligations and execute development projects. Turning to Delta State, Siakpere commended Governor Oborevwori for his investments in infrastructure, particularly road construction, bridges and flyovers. He said the engagement of reputable construction firms, including Julius Berger, reflected the administration’s determination to deliver durable infrastructure, adding that communities in Delta Central, including Okpe and neighbouring areas, were benefiting from ongoing projects. The APC chieftain urged party leaders in Aghalokpe to take the campaign to every ward, community and polling unit, ensuring that women, youths and first-time voters were actively involved. He also cautioned against internal wrangling and personal interests, calling for peaceful, issue-based campaigns capable of strengthening the party ahead of the elections.

item.title: Mock Accreditation: INEC Faces Crucial Test As 100 Million Voters Await 2027 Elections
item.description: With exactly 50 days before Nigerians return to the ballot, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is preparing for a nationwide test that could offer an important indication of whether the country is ready for another fiercely contested general election. On Saturday, November 28, the electoral umpire will deploy its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and electronic results upload technology across 17,676 selected polling units in a mock exercise designed to identify operational weaknesses, test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. The exercise, scheduled for 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., will cover two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas, giving INEC an opportunity to assess the performance of its electoral technology across different locations before the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, and the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6. #OsunDecides2026: Election Officers Take Delivery Of Materials, Mobilise To Polling Units during the Osun State governorship election on August 15, 2026. It comes against the backdrop of lingering controversies surrounding the 2023 general elections, particularly the failure to upload presidential election results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) in real time, technical difficulties associated with BVAS and allegations of electoral irregularities. Chairman of INEC, Joash Amupitan, described the mock exercise as an important part of preparations for the forthcoming elections, while urging Nigerians to participate. The commission’s Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria Meci, explained that the exercise would allow INEC to establish the effectiveness and reliability of its equipment before election day. “We don’t want to wait till the elections before we test the ruggedness, readiness and functionality of the system,” she said during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . According to her, the commission has reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS device, with additional machines to be provided at polling units with larger voter populations. The exercise will also test the electronic upload of results to IReV, although Meci acknowledged that successful transmission would depend on network availability. 100 Million Voters, 176,846 Polling Units The scale of the preparations reflects the size of Nigeria’s electorate. INEC says it is now managing a verified national register of more than 100 million voters after removing over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated, and deceased records from the previous register of approximately 103 million. Amupitan disclosed on Wednesday, during a meeting with resident electoral commissioners from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, that the clean-up followed the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System and a statutory claims-and-objections audit.
